import MumfordLib.LatticeTorus
import MumfordLib.ComplexUniformization
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Complex.Circle

/-!
# Topological coordinates from a full period lattice

The lattice-basis coordinates induce a homeomorphism from the actual period
quotient to a finite product of circles. Its underlying equivalence is the
additive quotient equivalence used for the torsion calculation.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

noncomputable section

namespace Mumford.Uniformization

namespace ComplexVectorLatticeExponentialData

variable {V X : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [NormedSpace ℂ V]
  [AddCommGroup X] [TopologicalSpace X] {g : ℕ}
  (d : ComplexVectorLatticeExponentialData V X g)

@[simp]
theorem quotientGenusTorusAddEquiv_mk (v : V) :
    d.quotientGenusTorusAddEquiv (QuotientAddGroup.mk' d.ambientPeriodLattice v) =
      genusTorusExponential g (d.latticeCoordinate v) := rfl

@[simp]
theorem quotientGenusTorusAddEquiv_symm_exponential (v : GenusRealVector g) :
    d.quotientGenusTorusAddEquiv.symm (genusTorusExponential g v) =
      QuotientAddGroup.mk' d.ambientPeriodLattice (d.latticeCoordinate.symm v) := by
  apply d.quotientGenusTorusAddEquiv.injective
  rw [quotientGenusTorusAddEquiv_mk]
  simp

/-- The lattice-basis coordinates are continuous in both directions. -/
def latticeCoordinateContinuousLinearEquiv : V ≃L[ℝ] GenusRealVector g := by
  letI : NormedSpace ℝ V := NormedSpace.restrictScalars ℝ ℂ V
  letI : FiniteDimensional ℝ V :=
    FiniteDimensional.of_injective d.latticeCoordinate.toLinearMap
      d.latticeCoordinate.injective
  exact d.latticeCoordinate.toContinuousLinearEquiv

/-- The lattice quotient equivalence is continuous. -/
theorem quotientGenusTorusAddEquiv_continuous : Continuous d.quotientGenusTorusAddEquiv := by
  rw [(QuotientAddGroup.isQuotientMap_mk d.ambientPeriodLattice).continuous_iff]
  change Continuous (fun v : V => genusTorusExponential g (d.latticeCoordinate v))
  exact (genusTorusExponential_continuous g).comp
    d.latticeCoordinateContinuousLinearEquiv.continuous

/-- The inverse lattice quotient equivalence is continuous. -/
theorem quotientGenusTorusAddEquiv_symm_continuous :
    Continuous d.quotientGenusTorusAddEquiv.symm := by
  rw [(genusTorusExponential_isOpenQuotientMap g).isQuotientMap.continuous_iff]
  change Continuous (fun v : GenusRealVector g =>
    d.quotientGenusTorusAddEquiv.symm (genusTorusExponential g v))
  simp_rw [d.quotientGenusTorusAddEquiv_symm_exponential]
  exact QuotientAddGroup.continuous_mk.comp
    d.latticeCoordinateContinuousLinearEquiv.symm.continuous

/-- Real lattice coordinates identify the period quotient homeomorphically
with the standard genus torus. -/
def quotientGenusTorusHomeomorph : (V ⧸ d.ambientPeriodLattice) ≃ₜ GenusTorus g :=
  { d.quotientGenusTorusAddEquiv with
    continuous_toFun := d.quotientGenusTorusAddEquiv_continuous
    continuous_invFun := d.quotientGenusTorusAddEquiv_symm_continuous }

@[simp]
theorem quotientGenusTorusHomeomorph_apply (q : V ⧸ d.ambientPeriodLattice) :
    d.quotientGenusTorusHomeomorph q = d.quotientGenusTorusAddEquiv q := rfl

end ComplexVectorLatticeExponentialData

/-- The additive-circle model of a genus torus is homeomorphic to the usual
finite product of unit circles. -/
def genusTorusCircleHomeomorph (g : ℕ) : GenusTorus g ≃ₜ (Fin (2 * g) → Circle) :=
  Homeomorph.piCongrRight fun _ => AddCircle.homeomorphCircle (by norm_num : (1 : ℝ) ≠ 0)

end Mumford.Uniformization
